title: Double Reverse Sear Steak
summary: Nearly no gray steak sear. Requires skillet, oven, and high smoke point oil.
profile: Pure beef and salt: a smoking-hot pan lays down a dark, crisp crust first, then a very low 215°F (100°C) oven brings the center up so gently that the pink runs almost edge to edge, with nearly no gray band under the crust. Texture target: tender and juicy, finished at about 120°F (49°C) in the center after the rest, which is rare to medium-rare; the oil is only there to carry the heat. Delivers one 12-oz steak for 2 in about 40 minutes, most of it hands-off while the oven and the rest do the work; slice against the grain and serve right away. Leftover slices keep 3 days refrigerated; eat them cold or warm them gently so they stay pink.

steps.text: Heat skillet on high heat with canola oil.
Thoroughly remove moisture and generously salt steak.
steps.tip: Salt the steak right before placing it in the pan to minimize surface moisture.

steps.text: When oil is highly smoking, sear steak on both sides for 1 minute each to achieve a near complete sear.
steps.tip: Note that the steak will continue to sear in the oven.

steps.text: Immediately place hot skillet with steak into heated oven. Flip when core temperature reaches 85°F (29°C).
steps.tip: Use an oven-safe skillet (cast iron or carbon steel); the handle comes out of the oven hot, so grab it with a towel or mitt.

steps.text: Remove steak when it reaches 105°F (41°C) internal temperature and let it sit until it reaches 120°F (49°C).
steps.tip: The heat stored in the crust keeps cooking the center while it sits, and the rest lets the juices settle so they stay in the steak when you slice it.

changelog.summary: Enriched: added the profile and tips for the oven-safe skillet and the rest; wrote the temperatures as °F (°C) (215°F, 85°F, 105°F, 120°F were saved without the degree sign); fixed "moister" → "moisture". Your amounts, wording and steps are unchanged.
